headline: Tech companies are replacing government functions and ushering in tyranny, says historian
summary: Harvard historian Jill Lepore warns that Silicon Valley's growing influence is a return to 'rule by algorithms, corporations, machines,' replacing democratic governance.
details: Harvard historian Jill Lepore, author of "The Rise and Fall of the Artificial State," argues that tech companies are increasingly taking over the roles traditionally held by democratic governments.

She warns this shift marks a dangerous return to 'tyranny and mystification' through rule by algorithms and corporations, a future she believes is being driven by leaders misinterpreting science fiction.
Lepore clarifies she is not anti-technology but objects to private corporations assuming state functions without public consent, a gradual transformation that has accelerated in the last 20-25 years.
The historian traces the idea of an 'artificial state' through centuries of thought and science fiction, suggesting that this model of governance is inherently unsustainable and ultimately fails.
Lepore also discussed the irony of Elon Musk's actions contradicting his political beliefs and criticized the notion of platforms like Twitter being digital town halls.
caption:
Silicon Valley is replacing democratic government with an 'artificial state,' warns Pulitzer Prize-winning historian Jill Lepore.

Harvard historian Jill Lepore, author of "The Rise and Fall of the Artificial State," argues that tech companies are increasingly taking over the roles traditionally held by democratic governments.

She warns this shift marks a dangerous return to 'tyranny and mystification' through rule by algorithms and corporations, a future she believes is being driven by leaders misinterpreting science fiction.

Lepore clarifies she is not anti-technology but objects to private corporations assuming state functions without public consent, a gradual transformation that has accelerated in the last 20-25 years.

The historian traces the idea of an 'artificial state' through centuries of thought and science fiction, suggesting that this model of governance is inherently unsustainable and ultimately fails.

Lepore also discussed the irony of Elon Musk's actions contradicting his political beliefs and criticized the notion of platforms like Twitter being digital town halls.
